task_instance: Given a small sample repo (Node/Express API + Vite/React frontend + docker-compose.yml declaring a Postgres service), run `aspire init` to drop the AppHost skeleton, then follow the aspireify workflow to wire the TypeScript AppHost (apphost.mts) with addProject/addPostgres/addViteApp resources and validate with `aspire start --non-interactive`.
blocker_detail: The skill's own prerequisite step (`aspire init`, which must succeed before aspireify has anything to wire) never completes in this runtime. The Aspire CLI (13.5.4, installed successfully via `npm install -g @microsoft/aspire-cli`, which does work since registry.npmjs.org is allow-listed) internally shells out to an 'aspire-managed' .NET process that must restore NuGet packages (Aspire.Hosting, Aspire.Hosting.CodeGeneration.TypeScript) from https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json and https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_packaging/dotnet9/nuget/v3/index.json even for the TypeScript AppHost path. The sandbox's egress proxy rejects both hosts with 403 (organization policy connect_rejected), confirmed via `curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status` showing repeated connect_rejected entries for pkgs.dev.azure.com and aspire.dev. `aspire init` hung indefinitely retrying this restore and had to be killed; no apphost.mts, apphost.ts, or aspire.config.json was ever produced (only a partial .aspire/integrations/package-restore cache directory). Without a dropped skeleton, aspireify's detection/edit/validate workflow (scanning for an unwired AppHost, editing apphost.mts, running `aspire start --non-interactive`) has no target to operate on. Separately, the .NET 10 SDK required for the C# AppHost path is also not installed and its own install path (dotnet.microsoft.com) is likewise not on the proxy allow-list, so the C# route is equally blocked.
evidence: Installed CLI: `npm install -g @microsoft/aspire-cli` succeeded (registry.npmjs.org is allow-listed); `aspire --version` -> 13.5.4+9c1b401dd67746739044f68959cbf4d3d7af93a6. Built sample repo at .../sample-repo with api/package.json (express+pg), web/package.json (vite+react), docker-compose.yml (postgres + api). Ran `aspire init --language typescript --non-interactive --suppress-agent-init --nologo`; process spawned aspire-managed which ran `nuget restore ... --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json --source https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_packaging/dotnet9/nuget/v3/index.json` and hung for minutes with no progress; had to be force-killed (exit 144). `curl -sS $PROXY/__agentproxy/status` output listed repeated `{"kind":"connect_rejected","detail":"gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)","host":"pkgs.dev.azure.com:443"}` and earlier attempts to reach aspire.dev and nuget.org directly also failed with connect_rejected. Post-mortem `find sample-repo/.aspire` showed only a package-restore cache skeleton, no apphost.mts/aspire.config.json — confirming `aspire init` never finished. No `dotnet` binary present (`which dotnet` -> not found), so the C# AppHost path was also unavailable as a fallback.
